01 / About

Securing agents.
Building intelligence
we can trust.

I am an Assistant Professor at Northern Arizona University. AI agent security is a central focus of my research: how prompt injection and untrusted tool outputs change an agent's behavior, where attacks enter an agent trajectory, and how to detect and localize failures. My broader work spans natural language processing, fact verification, quantum natural language processing, and access to AI resources.

I lead KALI Lab—Knowledge, Adversaries, Language & Intelligence—where we investigate secure, trustworthy tool-using agents alongside language understanding and emerging computational approaches.

02 / Research

AI agent security
and beyond.

Secure autonomous agents lead a research program spanning language understanding and emerging computational methods.

01

AI agent security

Detecting and localizing prompt-injection attacks in agent trajectories, and understanding when an agent resists or drifts from its intended task.

02

Language & reasoning

Fact verification, knowledge distillation, causal reasoning, and more transferable language systems.

03

Quantum language

Compositional and multilingual foundations for quantum natural language processing.

04 / Teaching

Courses for a
thinking future.

Public course overviews for students exploring AI, deep learning, and responsible intelligent systems.

CS 102 · Fall 2026

Introduction to AI

AI literacy for a world shaped by intelligent systems.

3 creditsNo prerequisites
Course overview

This interdisciplinary course builds a foundation in artificial intelligence, machine learning, data analytics, and responsible use. Students examine how AI systems work, where bias and privacy risks arise, and how AI is changing healthcare, transportation, creativity, and work.

Learning arc

  • AI concepts: machine learning, neural networks, computer vision, and NLP
  • Applications: search, recommendations, chatbots, assistants, and robotics
  • Society: bias, fairness, privacy, accountability, and trust
  • Practice: an ethical AI integration project in a domain of the student’s choice

Assessment

10%Attendance20%Quizzes30%Assignments40%Final project
CS 599 · Spring 2026

Deep Learning

Neural networks and natural language processing from first principles to practice.

3 creditsPython + data structures
Course overview

This course bridges the theory and practice of deep learning with applications to natural language processing. Students move from perceptrons and logistic regression to recurrent networks, transformers, language models, and practical systems built with PyTorch and Hugging Face.

Learning arc

  • Foundations: perceptrons, logistic regression, and feed-forward networks
  • Representations: distributional semantics and word embeddings
  • Sequence models: recurrent networks, contextual embeddings, and transformers
  • Applications: text classification, tagging, machine translation, and LLM inference

Assessment

20%Midterm 120%Midterm 225%Final exam10%Homeworks5%Paper readings20%Final project
